sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion at this exact site
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface expression confirmed by FLAG detection in surface expression experiments; no functional assay reported for the tagged construct specifically.
sites.rationale: The ledger explicitly names a FLAG epitope inserted after K115 in the extracellular domain of full-length, membrane-anchored AJAP1. The human canonical sequence has K at position 114 (not 115); Python search shows K114 is the only K in the immediate vicinity and the 1-residue offset is consistent with a single indel between mouse and human sequences upstream of this site. The site lies 71 residues from the mature N-terminus and 169 residues from the TM boundary, well within the extracellular domain (44–282). A short ALFA-tag insert here is directly precedented by the published FLAG insertion. Full-length mouse AJAP1 (membrane-anchored) expressed in pCI vector with a FLAG epitope inserted after K115 (mouse numbering) in the extracellular domain, used for surface expression experiments. The paper (PMC11235169) uses mouse AJAP1; human canonical position 114 = K, position 115 = A; mouse K115 maps to human K114 by a 1-residue offset between orthologs. Python search confirmed K114 is the nearest K to the stated position 115 in the human sequence.

sources.claim: For surface expression experiments, a FLAG epitope was inserted after K115 in the extracellular domain of AJAP1.

sites.evidence_type: published tolerance of a different insertion (transposon, FP fusion)
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by split-GFP complementation assay; the construct reached the cell surface with the sfGFP1-10 fragment accessible extracellularly. No independent functional assay of AJAP1 activity reported for this construct.
sites.rationale: The ledger explicitly names R170 as the junction for a large sfGFP1-10 domain insertion (flanked by G-S linkers) in the extracellular domain of full-length, membrane-anchored AJAP1. Python lookup confirms human position 170 = R, matching the paper exactly. The site is 127 residues from the mature N-terminus and 113 residues from the TM boundary. If the extracellular domain tolerates a ~230 aa sfGFP1-10 insertion here, a ~15–23 aa ALFA tag with GS linkers is sterically far less demanding and is well-supported at this junction. Full-length mouse AJAP1 (membrane-anchored, pCI-AJAP1-mCherry backbone) with superfolder GFP1-10 flanked by G-S linkers inserted after R170 in the extracellular domain, generating GN-AJAP1-mCherry used for split-GFP surface display detection. Human canonical position 170 = R, an exact match to the paper's stated R170; no numbering repair needed.

sources.claim: GN-AJAP1-mCherry and GN-AJAP1-SDBM-mCherry (containing superfolder GFP1–10 (44967, Addgene) flanked by G-S linkers after AJAP1-R170) were generated using the insert as a polymerase chain reaction primer with pCI-AJAP1-mCherry or pCI-AJAP1-SDBM-mCherry as templates.

literature_notes: Three ledger lines were evaluated. L3 (FLAG after K115/K114) and L2 (sfGFP1-10 after R170) both ground extracellular internal sites in full-length, membrane-anchored AJAP1 constructs and are reported above. L1 (C-terminal HA-mCherry) grounds only an intracellular tag (the C-terminus falls in the cytoplasmic domain, residues 304–411) and is recorded in other_positions. The K115 (mouse) → K114 (human) offset was resolved by Python search: human position 115 = A, position 114 = K; the 1-residue discrepancy is consistent with a single indel between mouse and human AJAP1 upstream of this site. No ledger evidence supports a tag at the mature N-terminus (residue 44) or any other extracellular position.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal HA-mCherry fusion on full-length AJAP1; the C-terminus lies in the intracellular domain (304–411) and is not accessible on the extracellular face.
